elements.element: Preferred: no liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment" — a Customer-payable liquidated amount survives

elements.element: Preferred: no penalties payable by Customer
elements.evidence: Termination Payment remains due on ordinary Company termination, payable "in eight (8) equal payments"

elements.element: Fallback: the Customer-payable liquidated amount is an early-termination fee (triggered by termination)
elements.evidence: "In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment"

elements.element: Fallback: that fee is capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "equal to the lesser of (i) ... and (ii) the aggregate fees payable by the Company to HDI under Section 3.1 in respect of the three (3) calendar months preceding the Termination Date"

elements.element: Fallback: it is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer on termination
elements.evidence: "the Termination Payment shall be the only amount payable by the Company by reason of termination"

offending_extra_words: No Termination Payment shall be due if the Company terminates this Agreement pursuant to Section 1.6 or as a result of HDI's breach of this Agreement,
reasons: Fallback is complete on its material terms: the lesser-of operator ensures the Termination Payment can never exceed three months' Section 3.1 fees, and the added sentence makes it the exclusive termination amount.
Preferred (no liquidated amount at all) is not met, which is expected given the locked fallback target.

Minimality fails: the edit adds a new carve-out (termination under Section 1.6 or for HDI's breach) that the fallback does not require, expanding 34 words to 107 and rewriting the operative measure rather than inserting a tight cap; a shorter '; provided that the Termination Payment shall not exceed three (3) months' fees under Section 3.1 and shall be the sole amount payable on termination' would suffice.
Cross-references to 'Section 1.6' and 'Section 3.1' are not verifiable from the supplied text; if either is misnumbered the carve-out and the cap measure would dangle.
Paragraph (c) instalment mechanic and the $800,000 deduction are left untouched, so unrelated commercial terms remain effective.
